page: Microsoft Azure E64ads_v7 is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor using the x86_64 architecture. Virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 64 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 32 physical cores with 2 threads per core at clock frequencies up to 4.5 GHz. The CPU features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, as well as hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives like AES and SHA-NI.

The hardware configuration provides 512.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio suitable for heavy in-memory operations. Fast ephemeral storage is directly included as a 3780 GB NVMe SSD. In synthetic evaluations, the platform demonstrates top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng and PassMark CPU metrics, coupled with top-tier PassMark memory and database operation scores. Large-block uncached memory bandwidth reaches 205.73 GB/sec for reads and 132.97 GB/sec for writes.

While lacking hardware GPU acceleration, the 64 vCPUs deliver strong small and medium language model inference processing, achieving top-tier throughput on models up to 7 billion parameters. On larger 70-billion-parameter models, execution speeds moderate to average tiers due to CPU compute boundaries. With substantial NVMe capacity and memory density per vCPU, the instance delivers high compute and memory efficiency for in-memory databases, large-scale Redis deployments, caching layers, and high-throughput transactional database workloads.
description: Microsoft Azure E64ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running up to 4.5 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system incorporates 32 physical cores with multithreading, advanced vector instructions including AVX-512, and 512.0 GB of RAM, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU profile. Storage is provisioned via an integrated 3780 GB NVMe SSD, avoiding external latency for temporary scratch and caching spaces. In benchmark testing, the platform achieves top-tier results in single-thread stress tests, PassMark CPU benchmarks, PassMark memory performance, and database operations, alongside recording 103.04 million Redis SET operations per second. While GPU acceleration is absent, the machine maintains robust CPU-based text generation for small and medium language models. This instance is configured for large transactional databases, distributed in-memory data grids, Redis clusters, and heavy memory-bound analytics pipelines.
